title: Identifier and secret components of one credential
description: A credential whose use needs more than one value: an identifier (account, key or client id) plus a secret, sometimes also a session token. The values can appear together, in either order, on separate lines, repeated, or with one component missing.
semantics: The expectation is stated per component, not per bundle: the secret component is the span that must be flagged; an identifier that travels with it is a companion span whose own confidentiality is a per-family question and is never assumed harmless or secret. When a provider does not state whether a component is confidential on its own, that case stays not-assertable rather than inheriting the secret's outcome. Whether a pair is complete, and how a consumer relates two spans, is not expressed by the current schema (span roles are secret and companion only); see the PR notes for the contract proposal.

applicability.rationale: Any family whose provider issues an identifier and a secret that are used together. The reasoning (state the secret span, keep the companion identifier separate, do not infer confidentiality of the companion) is the same for each; the per-family facts live in the cases.

evidenceBasis.rationale: The scenario states a project rule of how component-level expectations are written. Question: should a pair be one bundle span or per-component spans. Options: whole-bundle expectation; per-component expectation with companions. Chosen: per-component, because provider documents state secrecy per component (for example the AWS and Twilio pages cited by the cases). Would reverse if a consumer contract needs a bundle-level relation and a reviewed schema adds one. Each case carries its own provider evidence.

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed.
